title: Icon Oncology opens upgraded radiotherapy centre at Life Groenkloof Hospital in South Africa
summary: The centre features South Africa’s first iRT Systems Integral Quality Monitor (IQM), which independently checks radiation delivery during every treatment session.

contentHtml:
SOUTH AFRICA—Icon Oncology has officially opened its refurbished Groenkloof Radiation Oncology Centre at Life Groenkloof Hospital, expanding access to advanced cancer treatment through upgraded radiotherapy equipment and treatment monitoring technology.

The centre features South Africa’s first iRT Systems Integral Quality Monitor (IQM), which independently checks radiation delivery during every treatment session.

It also houses a new Elekta Versa HD linear accelerator, supported by Vision RT’s AlignRT surface-guided radiotherapy system.

The project involved refurbishing the treatment bunker and redesigning patient areas.

Icon Oncology operates the centre in partnership with De Mûelenaere Oncology (DMO), a radiation oncology practice that has served patients in Gauteng since 1976.

Integrated breast cancer care

The upgrade follows another development at Life Groenkloof Hospital.

In September 2026, its Breast Cancer Unit, led by clinical director Dr Marlene Soares, received certification from the European Society of Breast Cancer Specialists (EUSOMA).

According to the certification announcement, it is the first breast centre in Africa to receive this recognition.

The certification followed years of work to establish structured clinical pathways, multidisciplinary meetings and performance monitoring against EUSOMA’s international quality indicators.

The unit brings together breast surgeons, radiologists, pathologists, oncologists, nurses and support teams to coordinate patient care.

The upgraded radiotherapy facility extends this multidisciplinary approach to cancer treatment.

Patients with left-sided breast cancer can access breath-hold radiotherapy guided by surface cameras, a technique that helps reduce radiation exposure to the heart.

“Every woman who comes to us knows that her care is planned by a full team of specialists and measured against international standards,” said Dr Soares.

She noted that the upgraded equipment would help improve treatment precision and protect patients from potential long-term complications.

Technology partnerships and industry investment

The project took nearly a year to complete and involved collaboration between DMO’s radiation oncologists, Icon Oncology’s medical physics and radiotherapy teams, and three technology manufacturers.

Elekta supplied the Versa HD linear accelerator, Vision RT developed the AlignRT surface guidance system, while Germany-based iRT Systems provided the IQM technology.

Nexeva Health Solutions, the local distribution and technical support partner for the three manufacturers, integrated the systems and will provide ongoing maintenance and technical assistance.

According to Icon Oncology managing director of clinical operations Dr Cindy Aitton, the investment aims to bring advanced cancer treatment closer to patients while improving access to coordinated specialist care.

Nexeva managing director Simon Meredith said the company’s role extended beyond equipment installation to providing local engineering and clinical support to maintain system performance.

The opening ceremony, hosted by Dr Soares, brought together DMO oncologists, referring specialists, Icon Oncology executives, clinical teams and shareholders.

Guest speaker Wesley Naidoo, Vision RT’s director of clinical applications for EMEIA, discussed the role of surface-guided radiotherapy in improving treatment positioning and precision.

The investment forms part of Icon Oncology’s wider expansion of radiotherapy infrastructure across South Africa.

The group previously upgraded its Sandton and Arcadia Oncology Centres in 2024, followed by the Wilgers Oncology Centre in 2025.
